(infrastructure support and adjacent technical operations) to broaden the portfolio beyond traditional customer operations|AI positioned as a key strategic growth driver across Customer Operations, embedding intelligent automation, predictive analytics, conversational AI and real-time decision support into service delivery|Continued investment in the global delivery network, further strengthening strategic delivery locations such as Manila, Cairo and Lima|Continuously strengthening perimeter and internal security infrastructure (IAM rollout, PAM, SIEM, email security) to scale in step with the growing hybrid workforce|eClerx maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, considering financial parameters and internal/external factors when deciding between distribution and retention of profits; the Board's stated intent is to maintain its historical dividend payout ratio, exploring efficient methods to do so. During the year, the Company also returned surplus funds to shareholders via a share buyback, with the bought-back shares extinguished and paid-up capital reduced accordingly. Profit for the year was retained by carrying it forward to Retained Earnings rather than transferring it to General Reserve.
currentContext.expansion: eClerx continued to expand its global delivery footprint during FY26. In BFSI, it established a new team in Lima, Peru and grew its onshore teams in Singapore and London, while its Fayetteville Center of Excellence for Financial Crime and Compliance continued to scale, adding new clients and broadening client/functional diversification. In Cable, Media and Telecommunications, it continued to expand delivery capabilities in Manila, Cairo and Lima to support scalable, multilingual, digitally enabled customer operations; the Cairo site, within its first year of operations, became the top-performing site in the region for a global client. The company also launched advanced Network Operations Center (NOC) services for one of the world's largest global infrastructure companies. In the Emerging vertical, an additional floor was taken up in Manila to support strong growth in Finance and Accounting services. In Fashion & Luxury, new studio offerings were launched in Paris and Milan alongside AI-enabled creative services. On the technology side, eClerx launched Roboworx CogniFlows, its Enterprise AI orchestration platform with a pre-built agentic workbench, and established foundational partnerships with hyperscalers/AI platforms including Databricks and Adobe.

risks.note: Large clients possess greater bargaining power, which can result in pricing concessions, extended payment terms, or demands for additional scope at no incremental cost, compressing margins over time; deterioration, delayed payments, insolvency, or a change in control/strategy at a top client (e.g. insourcing or vendor consolidation) can lead to abrupt, largely uncontrollable loss of business.

The Company earned 87% of its revenue in US Dollars, 9% in Euros, and 4% in Sterling and other currencies, so exchange rate fluctuations can negatively impact financial performance; hedging strategies are used but do not eliminate the exposure.

The industry is highly competitive and evolving rapidly, with changing client expectations, new entrants, technology disruption and pricing pressure; low barriers to entry in certain segments allow well-funded technology-first players to disrupt traditional service models, particularly areas susceptible to automation or platform-based delivery.

Legislation in some client countries may restrict outsourcing of work to overseas entities like eClerx, which could hamper growth in major markets; withdrawal or material alteration of export/tax incentives, and evolving regulation around AI, cybersecurity, sanctions, employment and data protection, could increase compliance obligations, operational complexity and costs.

Rapid advances in automation, AI and digital tools are reshaping client expectations and service delivery models; competitors that adopt new technologies faster, or clients that build in-house automation, could reduce demand for traditional service offerings and erode eClerx's competitive positioning if it does not keep pace with innovation.

risks.risk: Cyber security incident / cyber attack risk
risks.note: The business relies extensively on IT systems and handles significant volumes of confidential client data; a breach (hacking, phishing, malware, insider threat, ransomware or DoS attack) could cause unauthorized data access/theft, breach client confidentiality agreements, trigger regulatory penalties and SLA/contractual liability, and reliance on third-party vendors/cloud providers adds exposure outside direct control.

The business is critically dependent on the quality, expertise and commitment of its workforce; inability to attract, develop, retain and motivate key talent could adversely affect service delivery quality, client expectations and long-term growth objectives.

Past or future acquisitions may pose financial, technological, operational and people integration risks; challenges integrating acquired businesses, personnel, technology platforms, internal controls and organizational cultures could divert management attention, disrupt ongoing business, increase costs, and expose the Company to cyber and information security risks.

one-line thesis: eClerx delivered record FY26 results with 17.9% USD revenue growth and 132 bps margin expansion, driven by a $90M analytics book and first large-scale Agentic AI wins, positioning it for top-quartile growth in FY27 despite macro headwinds. The strategic pivot to outcome-based AI services and diversification beyond BFSI reduces concentration risk while enhancing operating leverage.
financial scorecard: Revenue: USD 469M FY26 (+17.9% YoY), Q4 USD 122M (+17% YoY, +0.6% QoQ). EBITDA Margin: 25.7% Q4 (up 2.8% seq), FY26 expanded 132 bps. PAT: INR 706Cr FY26 (+30% YoY), Q4 INR 189.4Cr (16.7% margin). Order Book: New deals USD 46M in Q4; TTM bookings ~USD 170M (+24% YoY). Net Debt: Net cash positive; FCF INR 756Cr FY26. One-offs: Reclassification of business promotion expenses to subcontractor costs inflated subcon %; Bonus issue effective March impacted EPS calculation.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Top quartile of peer segment for FY27. Margin: 24%-28% EBITDA range maintained. Order Inflow: Aspiring for YoY growth in bookings (no specific % given). Capex: Increased in Q4 for computers/networking; no major commissioning projects cited.
order book & pipeline: Q4 new wins USD 46M; Analytics/Automation book at USD 90M; Strong pipeline in KYC, financial crime, and Agentic AI deployments starting Q1FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: CMT: Seq growth >7%, expanding to Manila/Cairo/Fayetteville. BFSI: Soft Q4 but strong pipeline in European bank lifecycle & KYC. High-Tech: First Agentic AI wins. Retail/Fashion: Sluggish but CLX expected to return to growth H1FY27. F&A (Personiv): Strong growth for 3 consecutive quarters.
growth verticals / optionality: Agentic AI scaling across verticals; Market360 expansion into Fortune 1000 retail/CPG; FCC services outside financial services; Geographic diversification (Manila, Cairo).
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margin walk: Delivery costs flat; G&A down 80 bps (facilities/tech); S&D down 20 bps. Q4 pressure from headcount addition and travel costs. Wage hike impact FY27 Q1 est. 300-350 bps.
capex / expansion: Q4 increase driven by computers and networking equipment; no large-scale infrastructure capex mentioned.
capital allocation: Buybacks remain preferred option over dividends (Dividend INR 1/share proposed); ESOP trust bought INR 250Cr shares from market in FY26.
risks & watch-items: Proposed NPRM on offshore call restrictions (US telcos/cable); Regulatory stringency in BFSI; AI-driven deflation in contract values; High attrition (21%); FX hedging at INR 89 limits upside in FY27.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'top quartile' growth ambition; cautious on fashion/retail but optimistic on high-tech and FCC; transparent about AI deflationary pressures but framing them as opportunities for wallet share gain.
non-obvious takeaways: Shift to outcome-based pricing in AI projects (e.g., 50% cost reduction in KYC refresh) rather than pure FTE models; Internal adoption of 'Roboworx/Cogniflows' by 3,000+ employees driving productivity before client billing; Subcon expense spike was purely accounting reclassification, not operational shift.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for compliant, AI-driven KYC and financial crime solutions amid regulatory tightening | eClerx Services Ltd | beneficiary | High | Pole position in FCC; first large Agentic AI win secured; USD 90M analytics book provides visible runway. |
| US offshore outsourcing restrictions (NPRM) threatening contact center volumes | Pure-play voice BPO peers | loser | Med | eClerx has contingency plans and geographic diversification, but pure voice players lack this flexibility. |
| AI deflation reducing contract values for traditional IT services | Legacy IT service providers | loser | Med | eClerx's outcome-based model and domain expertise allow it to capture wallet share despite deflation, whereas pure labor arbitrage models suffer. |

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
